newsitem.title: INDIA: CIS, Africa keen to buy Indian rice.
newsitem.headline: CIS, Africa keen to buy Indian rice.

text.p: Indian rice exports are expected to pick up soon, with rising demand from the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) and growing interest in Africa, traders said on Thursday.
"There is good export demand for five percent broken non-Basmati rice from CIS countries," said Prem Garg, managing director of Sri Lal Mahal Overseas Ltd, a leading Delhi foodgrains exporter.
Garg said shipments of nearly 100,000 tonnes of rice had left the Indian ports for CIS countries and another 80,000 tonnes of rice were currently being loaded.
Traders said Indian rice exporters were also negotiating contracts with Ethiopia and Ghana. But they gave no details of the negotiations or the quantities involved.
They said the Indian rice harvest was largely over, and crop arrivals were good.
"Eighty percent of the rice harvest is over and nearly 10,000 to 15,000 tonnes of rice is arriving in the Indian markets every day," Garg said.
The Agriculture Ministry expects winter output to be around 71.27 million tonnes.
India harvests two rice crops every year, getting the bulk of output from the winter crop. Sowing for the winter crop begins in July and the harvest starts in October.
Traders said Indian five percent broken non-Basmati rice was quoted at $300 per tonne FOB, 10 percent at $285, 15 percent at $265 and 25 percent at $235 per tonne.
Rice exports currently were a bit sluggish due to higher prices in India compared to Vietnam, said Mohan Narang, an official with Satnam Overseas, a leading Delhi foodgrains exporter.
"But exports will pick up during December and January once the Vietnam rice stocks are over," Narang said.
